# Book I, Proposition 46

*A square on a given straight line*

[Euclid's proof](#euclids-proof) · [In Lean](#in-lean) · [What it rests on](#what-it-rests-on) · [Mishnah](#mishnah)

> On a given straight line to describe a square.

## Euclid's proof

<p align="center"><img src="../../figures/I/46.svg" alt="Euclid's figure for Proposition I.46, with Heath's letters" width="360"></p>

Let AB be the given straight line; thus it is required to describe a square on the straight line AB.

Let AC be drawn at right angles to the straight line AB from the point A on it [I. 11], and let AD be made equal to AB; through the point D let DE be drawn parallel to AB, and through the point B let BE be drawn parallel to AD. [I. 31]

Therefore ADEB is a parallelogram; therefore AB is equal to DE, and AD to BE. [I. 34]

But AB is equal to AD; therefore the four straight lines BA, AD, DE, EB are equal to one another; therefore the parallelogram ADEB is equilateral.

I say next that it is also right-angled.

For, since the straight line AD falls upon the parallels AB, DE, the angles BAD, ADE are equal to two right angles. [I. 29]

But the angle BAD is right; therefore the angle ADE is also right.

And in parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one another; [I. 34] therefore each of the opposite angles ABE, BED is also right.

Therefore ADEB is right-angled.

And it was also proved equilateral.

Therefore it is a square; and it is described on the straight line AB.

Q. E. F.

**How the Lean follows the text**

- **Done by `OnRay.exists_len_eq`.** "and let AD be made equal to AB…" Euclid makes AD equal to AB on the perpendicular AC, taking enough room to cut it off by I.3 for granted; Heath gives no reference here. `OnRay.exists_len_eq` finds D on the ray AC by a circle about A with distance AB, using Postulate 3; C need not lie beyond D.
- **Done by `Prop31.parallelogram`.** "through the point D let DE be drawn parallel to AB…" Euclid draws the two parallels and takes their meeting at E from the figure. The Lean draws DE by I.31, then `Prop31.parallelogram` draws BE and finds E by `Prop30.meet`, using I.30.

```lean
/-- On a given straight line to describe a square. -/
theorem Prop46 {A B P : Point} (hAB : A ≠ B) (hP : ¬ Collinear A B P) :
    ∃ D E : Point, Square A D E B ∧ SameSideOf D P A B ∧ SameSideOf E P A B := by
  -- Let AB be the given straight line; thus it is required to describe a square on the
  -- straight line AB.
  obtain ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB⟩ := Postulate1 A B hAB
  -- Let AC be drawn at right angles to the straight line AB from the point A on it [I. 11],
  obtain ⟨C, hCP, hAC⟩ := Prop11 hAB ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, hA_AB⟩ hP
  have hBAC : ∠ B A C = ∟ := hAC B ⟨AB, hA_AB, hB_AB, hB_AB⟩ hAB.symm
  -- and let AD be made equal to AB; through the point D let DE be drawn parallel to AB, and
  -- through the point B let BE be drawn parallel to AD. [I. 31]
  /- A circle about A with distance AB gives D on the ray AC (Postulate 3).
     C need not lie beyond D. -/
  obtain ⟨D, hD, hAD⟩ := OnRay.exists_len_eq hAB hCP.triangle.ne₁₃
  have hDP : SameSideOf D P A B := SameSideOf.of_onRay hD hCP
  have hABD : Triangle A B D := hDP.triangle
  obtain ⟨DE, hD_DE, hDE_AB⟩ := Prop31.line (hABD.off_line hA_AB hB_AB)
  /- DE meets the parallel BE at E (`Prop31.parallelogram`). -/
  obtain ⟨E, -, hDABE⟩ := Prop31.parallelogram hDE_AB hD_DE hA_AB hB_AB hAB
  -- Therefore ADEB is a parallelogram; therefore AB is equal to DE, and AD to BE. [I. 34]
  have hADEB : Parallelogram A D E B := hDABE.rotate.reverse
  have hDE : D ≠ E := hADEB.2.1
  have hEB : E ≠ B := hADEB.1.2.1
  obtain ⟨hAB_DE, hAD_BE, -, -, -⟩ := Prop34 hADEB
  -- But AB is equal to AD; therefore the four straight lines BA, AD, DE, EB are equal to one
  -- another; therefore the parallelogram ADEB is equilateral.
  have h₁ : ‖A D‖ = ‖D E‖ := hAD.trans hAB_DE
  have h₂ : ‖D E‖ = ‖E B‖ :=
    hAB_DE.symm.trans (hAD.symm.trans (hAD_BE.trans (len_symm B E)))
  have h₃ : ‖E B‖ = ‖B A‖ :=
    (len_symm E B).trans (hAD_BE.symm.trans (hAD.trans (len_symm A B)))
  -- I say next that it is also right-angled.
  have hright : ∠ B A D = ∟ ∧ ∠ A D E = ∟ ∧ ∠ D E B = ∟ ∧ ∠ E B A = ∟ := by
    -- For, since the straight line AD falls upon the parallels AB, DE, the angles BAD, ADE are
    -- equal to two right angles. [I. 29]
    have h29 : ∠ B A D + ∠ A D E = ∟ + ∟ :=
      Prop29.interior hADEB.2.symm.swap_left hADEB.sameSideOf.symm
    -- But the angle BAD is right; therefore the angle ADE is also right.
    have hBAD : ∠ B A D = ∟ := (angle_onRay_right hD hAB.symm).trans hBAC
    have hADE : ∠ A D E = ∟ := by
      rw [hBAD] at h29
      exact CommonNotion3 (c := ∟) (d := ∟) (by rw [add_comm]; exact h29) rfl
    -- And in parallelogrammic areas the opposite sides and angles are equal to one
    -- another; [I. 34] therefore each of the opposite angles ABE, BED is also right.
    obtain ⟨-, -, hBAD_DEB, hABE_ADE, -⟩ := Prop34 hADEB
    have hABE : ∠ A B E = ∟ := hABE_ADE.trans hADE
    have hBED : ∠ B E D = ∟ :=
      (angle_symm hEB.symm hDE).trans (hBAD_DEB.symm.trans hBAD)
    -- Therefore ADEB is right-angled.
    exact ⟨hBAD, hADE, (angle_symm hDE hEB.symm).trans hBED,
      (angle_symm hEB hAB).trans hABE⟩
  -- And it was also proved equilateral.
  have hequil : ‖A D‖ = ‖D E‖ ∧ ‖D E‖ = ‖E B‖ ∧ ‖E B‖ = ‖B A‖ := ⟨h₁, h₂, h₃⟩
  -- Therefore it is a square; and it is described on the straight line AB.
  have hsquare : Square A D E B := ⟨hequil.1, hequil.2.1, hequil.2.2, hright⟩
  have hEP : SameSideOf E P A B :=
    hADEB.rotate.rotate.rotate.sameSideOf.swap.symm.trans hDP
  exact ⟨D, E, hsquare, hDP, hEP⟩
  -- Q. E. F.
```

```lean
/-- Squares described on equal straight lines are equal. Euclid assumes this in
I.48 ("since DA is equal to AB, the square on DA is also equal to the square on
AB"). Heath reports, under I.46, that Proclus proves it. Each square is a
parallelogram (`Prop28.square`), so the diameter AC cuts it into the triangles
ABC and ACD, right-angled at B and D; and I.4 makes these equal to the triangles
A'B'C' and A'C'D'. Here a square ABCD is "described on AB" when its far corners
C, D lie on one side of AB. [I. 4, I. 28] -/
theorem Prop46.square_eq {A B C D A' B' C' D' : Point} (h : Square A B C D)
    (hCD : SameSideOf C D A B) (h' : Square A' B' C' D') (hCD' : SameSideOf C' D' A' B')
    (hAB : ‖A B‖ = ‖A' B'‖) : quadArea A B C D = quadArea A' B' C' D' := by
  have hp := Prop28.square h hCD
  have hp' := Prop28.square h' hCD'
  obtain ⟨h₁, h₂, h₃, -, hB, -, hD⟩ := h
  obtain ⟨h₁', h₂', h₃', -, hB', -, hD'⟩ := h'
  /- All four sides of each square are equal to its side AB. -/
  have hBC : ‖B C‖ = ‖B' C'‖ := h₁.symm.trans (hAB.trans h₁')
  have hCD₁ : ‖D C‖ = ‖D' C'‖ := by
    rw [len_symm D C, len_symm D' C', ← h₂, ← h₂']
    exact hBC
  have hDA : ‖D A‖ = ‖D' A'‖ := by
    rw [← h₃, ← h₃']
    exact (len_symm D C).symm.trans (hCD₁.trans (len_symm D' C'))
  have t₁ : △ B A C = △ B' A' C' :=
    (Prop4 hp.triangle.bac hp'.triangle.bac
      ((len_symm B A).trans (hAB.trans (len_symm A' B'))) hBC (hB.trans hB'.symm)).2.1
  have t₂ : △ D C A = △ D' C' A' :=
    (Prop4 hp.rotate.rotate.triangle.bac hp'.rotate.rotate.triangle.bac hCD₁ hDA
      (hD.trans hD'.symm)).2.1
  unfold quadArea
  rw [area_bac A B C, t₁, area_cba A C D, t₂, ← area_bac A' B' C', ← area_cba A' C' D']

/-- Conversely, equal squares are described on equal straight lines. Euclid assumes
this too in I.48 ("therefore the square on DC is equal to the square on BC, so that
the side DC is also equal to BC"). Heath reports, under I.46, Proclus' proof, which
places the two squares side by side and then reasons through I.39, I.27, I.34
and I.26. We take another road, because no rule of ours carries a square to a new
place (`Prop44.place` meets the same limit): one square has to be described
afresh, and described inside the other it is a part of it. Were AB less than
A'B', cut off from A'B' a straight line A'X equal to AB [I. 3], and describe on
it a square A'ZYX on the side of C' [I. 46]. It is equal to the square ABCD (`Prop46.square_eq`); Z
falls on A'D', short of D'; and each square is double the triangle its diameter
cuts off from A' [I. 34]. But the triangle XA'Z is a part of the triangle
B'A'D', and so less. [I. 3, I. 4, I. 28, I. 34, I. 46] -/
theorem Prop46.side_eq {A B C D A' B' C' D' : Point} (h : Square A B C D)
    (hCD : SameSideOf C D A B) (h' : Square A' B' C' D') (hCD' : SameSideOf C' D' A' B')
    (hsq : quadArea A B C D = quadArea A' B' C' D') : ‖A B‖ = ‖A' B'‖ := by
  /- The square on the less straight line is the less. -/
  have less : ∀ {A B C D A' B' C' D' : Point}, Square A B C D → SameSideOf C D A B →
      Square A' B' C' D' → SameSideOf C' D' A' B' → ‖A B‖ < ‖A' B'‖ →
      quadArea A B C D < quadArea A' B' C' D' := by
    intro A B C D A' B' C' D' h hCD h' hCD' hlt
    have hp' : Parallelogram A' B' C' D' := Prop28.square h' hCD'
    have hA'B' : A' ≠ B' := hCD'.1
    obtain ⟨L, hA'_L, hB'_L⟩ := Postulate1 A' B' hA'B'
    /- Cut off A'X equal to AB, and describe the square A'ZYX on it. -/
    obtain ⟨X, hA'XB', hA'X⟩ := Prop3 hCD.1 hlt
    have hX_L : OnLine X L := on_line_of_between_ends hA'XB' hA'_L hB'_L
    have hA'X_ne : A' ≠ X := ne_of_between hA'XB'
    have hC'_L : ¬ OnLine C' L := not_on_line_of_same_side (hCD'.sameSide hA'_L hB'_L)
    obtain ⟨Z, Y, hsqZ, hZ, hY⟩ :=
      Prop46 hA'X_ne fun ⟨K, hA'_K, hX_K, hC'_K⟩ =>
        hC'_L ((line_unique hA'X_ne hA'_K hX_K hA'_L hX_L) ▸ hC'_K)
    have hZY : SameSideOf Z Y X A' := (hZ.trans hY.symm).swap
    have hsq' : Square X A' Z Y := hsqZ.rotate.rotate.rotate
    have hps : Parallelogram X A' Z Y := Prop28.square hsq' hZY
    have heq : quadArea A B C D = quadArea X A' Z Y :=
      Prop46.square_eq h hCD hsq' hZY (hA'X.symm.trans (len_symm A' X))
    /- Z falls on A'D', short of D'. -/
    have hZD' : SameSideOf Z D' A' B' :=
      (SameSideOf.of_line hA'B' hA'_L hB'_L (hZ.sameSide hA'_L hX_L)).trans hCD'
    have hZray : OnRay Z A' D' := by
      refine onRay_of_angle_eq hZD' ?_
      rw [angle_onRay_left (OnRay.of_beyond hA'XB') hZD'.triangle.ne₁₃.symm, hsqZ.2.2.2.1,
        angle_symm hA'B'.symm hCD'.symm.triangle.ne₁₃.symm, h'.2.2.2.1]
    have hA'Z : ‖A' Z‖ < ‖A' D'‖ := by
      rw [hsqZ.1.trans (hsqZ.2.1.trans hsqZ.2.2.1), len_symm X A', hA'X, len_symm A' D',
        ← h'.2.2.1, ← h'.2.1, ← h'.1]
      exact hlt
    have hA'ZD' : Between A' Z D' :=
      hZray.between_of_len_lt (OnRay.self hCD'.symm.triangle.ne₁₃) hA'Z
    /- Each square is double the triangle its diameter cuts off from A'. -/
    have hbig : quadArea A' B' C' D' = △ B' A' D' + △ B' A' D' := by
      rw [← hp'.quadArea_rotate, ← quadArea_reverse B' C' D' A']
      exact Prop34.bisect hp'.reverse.rotate.rotate.rotate
    /- And the triangle XA'Z is a part of the triangle B'A'D'. -/
    have hpart : △ X A' Z < △ B' A' D' := by
      rw [area_cba X A' Z]
      refine lt_trans (area_lt_of_cut hZD'.triangle.cab hA'XB') ?_
      rw [area_cba Z A' B']
      exact area_lt_of_cut hCD'.symm.triangle.bac hA'ZD'
    rw [heq, Prop34.bisect hps, hbig]
    exact Magnitude.add_self_lt_add_self hpart
  rcases lt_trichotomy ‖A B‖ ‖A' B'‖ with hlt | heq | hgt
  · exact absurd hsq (Magnitude.ne_of_lt (less h hCD h' hCD' hlt))
  · exact heq
  · exact absurd hsq.symm (Magnitude.ne_of_lt (less h' hCD' h hCD hgt))
```

**Lengths, angles and areas**

- [`angle_add_of_inside`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L47): If D lies within the angle BAC, then BAC is made up of BAD and DAC. (Diagram-angle 2)
- [`angle_eq_of_same_rays`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L54) (through [`angle_onRay_right`](../../Elements/Figure/Angles.lean#L49)): The angle doesn't change if its arms are traced through other points on the same rays. (Diagram-angle 4)
- [`angle_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L27) (used here): The angle ABC is the angle CBA. (Metric 4)
- [`area_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L70): Cutting a triangle in two from a vertex adds up. (Diagram-area 2)
- [`area_congruent`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L41): Triangles equal in all their sides and angles are equal in area. Euclid uses this without comment once he has shown two triangles congruent. (Metric 9)
- [`area_degenerate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L33): A "triangle" with a repeated corner has no area. (Metric 6)
- [`area_eq_zero_of_on_line`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L62): A "triangle" whose corners lie on one straight line has no area. (Diagram-area 1)
- [`area_rotate`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L36): The triangle ABC is the triangle CAB. (Metric 8)
- [`circle_eq`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L30) (through [`OnRay.exists_len_eq`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L141), [`Prop29.interior`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop29.lean#L152), [`Prop31.line`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop31.lean#L79) and 5 other lemmas): A circle is fixed by its centre and its radius. (Diagram-segment 2)
- [`len_add_of_between`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L27) (through [`OnRay.exists_len_eq`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L141), [`Prop29.interior`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop29.lean#L152), [`Prop31.line`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop31.lean#L79) and 5 other lemmas): If B is between A and C, then AB and BC together make up AC. (Diagram-segment 1)
- [`len_self`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L21) (through [`OnRay.exists_len_eq`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L141), [`Prop29.interior`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop29.lean#L152), [`Prop31.line`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop31.lean#L79) and 5 other lemmas): The "straight line" from a point to itself has no length. (Metric 1)
- [`len_symm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Metric.lean#L24) (used here): The straight line AB is the straight line BA. (Metric 3)
- [`same_ray_of_angle_eq_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Transfer.lean#L42): If the angle BAC is nothing, C lies on the ray from A through B. (Diagram-angle 1)

**Superposition**

- [`superposition`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Superposition.lean#L48): **Superposition.** A hypothetical placement of a triangle on a given ray and side permits a restricted derivation of metric equalities about the figure already given. The derivation introduces no further objects, cites each geometric law it uses, and exports no symbol of the placement.

**Laws of magnitude**

- [`add_assoc`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L23) (through [`Prop29.interior`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop29.lean#L152)): Adding three magnitudes in a row, it makes no difference whether the first two or the last two are added first. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_comm`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L26) (used here): The order of adding does not matter. (System E §3.5)
- [`add_lt_add_right`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L45) (through [`OnRay.exists_len_eq`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L141) and [`Prop29.interior`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop29.lean#L152)): Adding the same thing to both sides keeps "less than". (System E §3.5)
- [`add_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L29): Adding nothing changes nothing. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_irrefl`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L32) (through [`OnRay.exists_len_eq`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L141), [`Prop29.interior`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop29.lean#L152), [`Prop31.line`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop31.lean#L79) and 5 other lemmas): No magnitude is less than itself. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trans`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L35) (through [`OnRay.exists_len_eq`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L141), [`Prop29.interior`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop29.lean#L152), [`Prop31.line`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop31.lean#L79) and 5 other lemmas): What is less than the less is less still. (System E §3.5)
- [`lt_trichotomy`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L39) (through [`OnRay.exists_len_eq`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L141), [`Prop29.interior`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop29.lean#L152), [`Prop31.line`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop31.lean#L79) and 5 other lemmas): Of two magnitudes, one is less, or they are equal, or the other is less. (System E §3.5)
- [`not_lt_zero`](../../Elements/Foundations/Tacit/Magnitudes.lean#L42) (through [`OnRay.exists_len_eq`](../../Elements/Figure/Rays.lean#L141), [`Prop29.interior`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop29.lean#L152), [`Prop31.line`](../../Elements/BookI/Prop31.lean#L79) and 5 other lemmas): Nothing is less than zero. (System E §3.5)

</details>

## Mishnah

_Our commentary: what Euclid assumes, what Lean made us say out loud, and how the result looks by modern means._

Proclus notes that Euclid constructs a triangle but describes a square on a straight line, and Heath puts the difference so: "The *triangle* (or *angle*) is, so to say, pieced together, while the describing of a square on a given straight line is the making of a figure 'from' *one* side, and corresponds to the multiplication of the number representing the side by itself" (vol. 1, p. 348). So Euclid builds ADEB from AB alone, with a right angle, an equal straight line and two parallels, and only then proves it a square: equilateral and right-angled, as Definition I.22 asks. One step goes unnamed: "the angle ADE is also right" takes the right angle BAD from two right angles, and that is Common Notion 3.

Euclid's figure settles which side of AB the square stands on; his enunciation is silent. In our statement a given point settles it, and D and E are promised on its side, because I.47 needs its squares outward and I.48 describes three of them so. I.11 draws AC on that side, and a circle about A lays off AD equal to AB (Post. 3). Heath draws C beyond D; our proof leaves their order open.

**Equal squares, equal sides.** Euclid takes for granted in I.48 that squares on equal straight lines are equal, and the converse. Heath reports Proclus proving both here (vol. 1, pp. 348–349), and we prove them after I.46 as `Prop46.square_eq` and `Prop46.side_eq`. The first, Heath says, "is immediately obvious if we divide the squares into two triangles by drawing a diagonal in each" (vol. 1, p. 348): I.4 makes the triangles equal. For the converse Proclus sets the squares side by side; we prove it where they stand. I.3 cuts off from the greater side a straight line equal to the less, I.46 describes a square on it inside the greater square, and by I.34 the half of the one is a part of the half of the other, and so less.

**The modern way.** In the complex plane, turning AB about A through $\pi/2$ gives AD: $\mathrm{D = A} + i\mathrm{(B - A)}$, and $\mathrm{E = B} + i\mathrm{(B - A)}$ completes the square ADEB. Multiplying by $-i$ instead describes the square on the other side of AB, and the given point says which.

## Further reading

- Multiplying by i turns the plane through a right angle, and Paul J. Nahin's [*An Imaginary Tale*](https://doi.org/10.1515/9781400833894) (2010) tells how mathematicians came to draw √−1 that way (also on [I.11](11.md)).
- More of Euclid's geometry done with complex numbers fills Liang-shin Hahn's [*Complex Numbers and Geometry*](https://doi.org/10.1090/text/052) (2019) (also on [I.9](09.md)).
